doc.title: Joe Wilder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: His own albums and the new quintet record
summary: He lists his albums and describes the new quintet album pushed by Ed Berger.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: You know what I didn’t ask you about? – I’m sorry. I should let you – . . .
. . . is your new album that just came out. You did one other album of your own.
I did – actually there’s two others.

For Columbia Records. I did – I’ve done three, actually, because I did a couple for Savoy Records. Then I did two for Columbia. Then the one with Benny Carter. Oh, and I did one with Joe Newman. We also did one together. Joe Newman and I did one together. It’s called Together Again. Then I just did this one.
What’s this latest one? What did you choose to put on that?

We have a few things that – I cannot remember actually what. I should have brought that with me. I had it. There was one of them sitting on the table when I left. We did a variety of things. We did Far Away Places. We did What a Wonderful World. I would really like that as a tribute to Louis Armstrong, because I think the way he did it is so touching, so beautiful. We did Answer Me, My Love, the Nat Cole thing.
How did you choose it? How did this album come about?

Ed Berger and Benny Carter thought that I should make one, particularly Ed Berger, who’s a very dear friend and one of the most compassionate guys in the world. He just kept saying, we’ve got to do this and we’ve got to do it, until finally we did it. Then he’s been running around like a chicken with his head cut off, pushing this thing. If you knew the amount of legwork that he’s put into it. I would have given up long ago. I would have said, “Look, Ed, let’s just play it a home and forget about it.” He has not given up a bit. He just stuck with it.
What was it like to do? Is this a solo album? Or do you have a regular . . . ?
I have – there are other fellows. It’s a quintet.
What was it like to put the album together?

It was fun. We did it over at RCA on 44th Street. It was nice. I would like to do an album in the future where we took time – had more time for preparation. We didn’t have as much time to prepare this as I had wished we had. I think it might have come off a little better had we had more time.
If you’d had a chance to rehearse it.
Yeah, but then it’s hard to do that too, because people are busy.
Yeah, and time is precious these days.
